system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41:50 UTC, ivy.chen's Word process opened C:\Users\ivy.chen\Downloads\Statement.docm from Explorer.

Two seconds later, Word launched PowerShell with no profile, a hidden window, and an encoded command. The command decodes to downloading and invoking a script from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nwd-it/tools/main/u.ps1.
The proxy recorded a successful GET (status 200) for that exact u.ps1 URL. The associated network activity includes a PowerShell connection to the proxy on source port 52805.

PowerShell then launched rundll32.exe with C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll,Init as its command. This sequence is consistent with executing code retrieved by the hidden PowerShell command and is strongly indicative of malicious activity.
The rundll32 process exited about 12 seconds after it started; PowerShell exited later, about 26 seconds after it started.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable on WS-NBLAKE-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC; other listed hosts and times were reported as collected successfully.
The evidence includes proxy metadata for the script request but not the response body, so the downloaded script's contents are not available here.
The supplied records do not include file-content or DLL-analysis evidence for svchelper.dll.
claims_not_established: The available records do not establish who created or delivered Statement.docm, or whether ivy.chen knowingly opened it or enabled its macro.
The downloaded u.ps1 contents and the behavior of svchelper.dll are not established by these records.
The records do not establish whether the DLL was successfully loaded or what actions it performed, including any persistence, credential access, lateral movement, or data theft.
The records do not establish whether other hosts or accounts were affected.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze Statement.docm, including its macro code and file provenance.
Retrieve the exact u.ps1 response, if available, and analyze its contents.
Acquire svchelper.dll from WS-ICHEN-01, preserve its metadata and hash, and analyze it.
Collect endpoint file, registry, module-load, and persistence evidence around the execution time, along with relevant Defender detections and quarantine records.
Review broader network and endpoint telemetry for follow-on activity and related indicators across other hosts.
